title: Retrenchment benefit payouts and whether rules should differ by company size
asked: For each year from 2020 to 2025, how many companies with more than 25 workers paid retrenchment benefits above the tripartite guidelines, and how many paid below them.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said that based on Mandatory Retrenchment Notification data from companies with 10 or more employees, around nine in 10 eligible employees received retrenchment benefits from 2020 to 2025, and around eight in 10 of those received at least two weeks' salary per year of service, in line with the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment. He said mandatory notification applies to companies retrenching five or more workers, not by company size. He said the tripartite partners deliberated on making retrenchment benefits mandatory and on setting a minimum quantum in law, and concluded that guidelines with flexibility would achieve better outcomes for workers and businesses.

key_points.point: Around nine in 10 eligible employees received retrenchment benefits from 2020 to 2025, based on MRN data from companies with 10 or more employees
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: around nine in 10 eligible employees received retrenchment benefits from 2020 to 2025

key_points.point: Around eight in 10 of those received at least two weeks' salary per year of service, in line with the tripartite advisory norms
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: around eight in 10 received retrenchment benefits of at least two weeks’ salary per year of service

key_points.point: Mandatory retrenchment notification applies to companies retrenching five or more workers, not by company size
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: our requirement for mandatory retrenchment is for companies that retrench five or more workers to notify MOM

key_points.point: The tripartite partners concluded that guidelines with business flexibility would achieve better outcomes than legislating benefits
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we concluded that a balanced approach to protect workers, while at the same time providing businesses flexibility, would achieve better outcomes for both workers and businesses

key_points.point: For unionised companies with a collective agreement, the prevailing norm is one month per year of service
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: for unionised companies, if they have a collective agreement, the prevailing norm in unionised companies with a collective agreement is one month per year of service

key_points.point: MOM does not hold a breakdown of how many of the eight in 10 received more than two weeks per year of service
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: I do not have the breakdown of how many among these eight in 10 received more than two weeks per year of service

key_points.point: The exact date of the last tripartite review of retrenchment benefits was not available, with TAMEM updated around the COVID-19 period
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: I am afraid I do not have the detail of the exact date in which we did this review

key_points.point: MOM encourages unions to engage multinationals that set retrenchment benefit caps below the benchmark
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we do encourage our unions to continue to engage with multinationals

left_open: Year-by-year figures from 2020 to 2025 for companies with more than 25 workers specifically
The number of companies paying above the prevailing guideline versus at the guideline
The exact date the tripartite partners last deliberated on retrenchment benefits
supplementary: Whether pre-retrenchment notification should be mandatory, whether punitive clauses should cost Work Pass privileges, and whether benefits should scale with company size.
